question: Can pattern matching in compositional tasks be defined by observed functional equivalence, used to predict instance-level success and data scaling, and separated from mechanisms that generalize beyond observed substitutions?

key_findings.claim: The paper defines functional equivalence through equal behavior of substituted input fragments across shared contexts and defines coverage as reachability in the induced substitution graph.
key_findings.evidence: Definitions 3.1-3.2 make pattern matching data-centered and model-agnostic: test items connected to training examples by sufficiently witnessed substitutions are inside k-coverage, while unreachable items are outside its evidential boundary.

key_findings.claim: Instance accuracy rises with the number of contexts supporting the required equivalence, and successful models cluster equivalent fragments in intermediate representations.
key_findings.evidence: Controlled 2-hop experiments stratify examples by k-coverage; intra-inter cosine gap increases with evidence strength, and causal tracing supports a functional role for the clustered representation.

key_findings.claim: For a uniform two-hop construction, the required sample size for perfect in-domain coverage has a tight polynomial exponent between 2 and 2.5 depending on the evidence threshold k.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 6.1 gives an approximately Theta(n^c) boundary with c=2.5-0.5/k up to polylog factors; measured 2-hop exponent 2.26 agrees, while parallel and 3-hop structures show steeper empirical exponents.

key_findings.claim: The measured data exponent is stable across a roughly 20-fold GPT-2 parameter range and a small Mamba, suggesting model scaling alone does not remove this pattern-matching data burden in the tested regime.
key_findings.evidence: Fits for GPT-2 from 68M to 1.5B parameters and the reported Mamba configuration all remain inside the theoretical range, with R-squared above 0.99 for the plotted fits.

key_findings.claim: Path ambiguity prevents a single intermediate-state representation when one variable affects the output through multiple routes.
key_findings.evidence: On NON-TREE, representations cluster by the context-conditioned pair (b,x2) rather than b alone; near-exhaustive data, prolonged training, 1.5B parameters, and Mamba do not recover the clean 2-hop behavior under standard training.

key_findings.claim: Chain-of-thought supervision lowers compositional data exponents but does not eliminate path ambiguity.
key_findings.evidence: CoT reduces the 3-hop exponent from 2.58 to 1.76 and aligns exponents across hop counts, yet NON-TREE still fails to match 2-HOP and retains x2-conditioned representation clusters.

key_findings.claim: The theory is conditional on a learner that generalizes only within k-coverage and therefore does not prove that trained transformers cannot use algebraic, operator-sharing, or other mechanisms beyond pattern matching.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 6.1 explicitly analyzes a coverage-constrained learner, and Section 9.2 introduces property-based and shared-operator generalization as separate mechanisms intentionally removed from the randomized tasks.

method.core_idea: Turn the vague claim that neural models pattern-match into a falsifiable, dataset-relative substitution criterion and isolate it on randomized compositional functions.
method.mechanism: Shared contexts witness fragment equivalence; those equivalences form graph edges; graph reachability defines coverage; controlled tree and non-tree functions manipulate the evidence available for equivalence; accuracy, representation clustering, causal tracing, and dataset scaling test the predictions.
assumptions: Random primitive functions remove exploitable algebraic and semantic structure.
Functional equivalence across observed contexts is the dominant mechanism in the controlled tasks.
Coverage threshold k adequately summarizes evidence strength.
Perfect in-domain generalization is an appropriate endpoint for the sample-complexity theorem.
Synthetic token-set scaling is informative about, but not identical to, natural-language reasoning.

techniques.role: Defines when two input fragments can be substituted based on shared-context behavior.
Maps observed equivalences into an instance-level generalization boundary.
Suppresses algebraic shortcuts so pattern matching can be isolated.
Quantifies clustering of equal intermediate states in hidden representations.
Tests whether clustered intermediate representations affect predictions.
Characterizes how data requirements grow with token-set size.

evaluations.setting: Decoder-only GPT-2 on 2-HOP randomized functions with examples partitioned by k-coverage.
evaluations.metric: Instance accuracy and intra-inter cosine gap.
evaluations.result: Greater functional-equivalence support predicts both higher accuracy and stronger hidden-state clustering; k=0 items lack the cluster pattern.
evaluations.baseline: Out-of-coverage examples and alternative representation groupings.

evaluations.setting: 2-HOP, PARALLEL-2-HOP, and 3-HOP across token-set sizes; GPT-2 68M-1.5B and a 4-layer Mamba.
evaluations.metric: Minimum data for at least 0.99 ID accuracy and log-log scaling exponent.
evaluations.result: 2-HOP measures c=2.26 within the theoretical range; more complex structures are steeper, and parameter scaling does not materially change the exponent.
evaluations.baseline: The theorem's coverage-driven exponent and alternative architectures/scales.

evaluations.setting: NON-TREE path-ambiguity task with up to near-exhaustive ID data and extended training.
evaluations.metric: ID accuracy and representation clustering by b versus (b,x2).
evaluations.result: Models fail to form a unified b state and instead encode context-conditioned states, even when one run reaches 0.96 after 36,000 epochs.

evaluations.setting: CoT-supervised 2-, 3-, and 5-hop tasks plus CoT NON-TREE.
evaluations.metric: Data-scaling exponent, ID accuracy, and IICG.
evaluations.result: CoT flattens hop-dependent data scaling but only partially improves NON-TREE and leaves context dependence.

limitations: The formal lower boundary applies to coverage-constrained learners, not all possible transformer algorithms.
Experiments use random synthetic functions without natural-language semantics or pretrained knowledge.
The primary target is in-domain combination coverage rather than robust out-of-distribution reasoning.
Reported architecture diversity is limited to decoder GPT-2 variants and one relatively small Mamba.
The k threshold compresses heterogeneous contextual evidence into one count.
The proposed mapping to planning, reversal, and negation failures remains a hypothesis requiring task-level tests.
failure_modes: A variable appearing on multiple paths prevents fragments from being globally substitutable.
Coverage can be high while representations remain context-bound and mechanistically opaque.
Parameter scaling does not change a data-combinatorics bottleneck in the tested range.
CoT can expose intermediate outputs yet still preserve entangled state representations.
Logit-lens-style vocabulary projection can miss intermediate clusters not aligned with token embeddings.
Training distributions with poor shared-context diversity fail to witness needed equivalences.
reusable_insights: Define a proposed generalization mechanism by what substitutions its evidence licenses before measuring behavior.
Distinguish dataset size from coverage diversity: shared contexts can be the scarce resource.
Test latent-state identity with both geometric probes and causal interventions.
Use path multiplicity as a structural stress test for intermediate-state representations.
Treat CoT as a change to supervision and computation structure, not a universal cure for compositionality.
open_questions: Can coverage be estimated for semantic fragments in natural corpora?
Which architectural biases explicitly unify states across path ambiguity?
How do property-based and shared-operator generalization interact quantitatively with functional equivalence?
Does pretraining change the exponent by importing equivalences or a distinct algorithm?
Can data selection maximize equivalence coverage under a fixed token budget?
What causal circuits implement substitution reachability across model families?

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Capabilities of Autoregressive Transformers: A Study on Synthetic, Interpretable Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ramesh et al. show positive combinatorial composition and benefits from intermediate outputs; the target explains a narrower pattern-matching regime through functional-equivalence coverage and constructs path ambiguity as a boundary.

competitive_landscape.title: When can transformers compositionally generalize in-context?
competitive_landscape.difference: Kobayashi et al. find an explicit inference/execution bottleneck enables in-context compositionality; the target locates a data-evidence and path-ambiguity boundary under ordinary end-to-end training.

competitive_landscape.title: Dissecting Chain-of-Thought: Compositionality through In-Context Filtering and Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. explain CoT through stepwise filtering and in-context learning of simpler functions; the target empirically confirms lower exponents but shows explicit steps do not remove multi-path state ambiguity.

competitive_landscape.title: The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on A is B fail to learn B is A
competitive_landscape.relationship: realistic behavioral failure explained by the framework
competitive_landscape.difference: Berglund et al. establish a directional factual generalization failure; the target offers functional-equivalence coverage as a possible mechanism but does not directly re-run the factual experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: Data Factors for Better Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. empirically vary data complexity, diversity, and difficulty across compositional benchmarks; the target supplies a sharper substitution-coverage variable and a theorem for one controlled family.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Functional equivalence supplies a predictive definition of pattern matching, a tight two-hop data-scaling law, and a new path-ambiguity failure mode.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Formal coverage definitions, upper/lower sample bounds, 20x parameter-scale experiments, representation analyses, causal tracing, and CoT ablations align on controlled tasks.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The data-relative formalization and path-ambiguity diagnostic are strong and meaningfully sharper than prior qualitative pattern-matching claims. Novelty should remain scoped to randomized controlled tasks and coverage-constrained generalization rather than a universal theory of LLM reasoning.
